title: Legacy Chat schema translator for OpenAI ChatCompletions → Redwood streaming + tools
creator: Aisha Karim
description: Implement a compatibility layer that translates incoming OpenAI ChatCompletions v1 requests into Redwood's internal streaming + function-calling / structured-output request format and maps responses back to OpenAI-compatible responses. This covers both non-streaming and streaming paths, tool/function call semantics, and structured output (JSON schemas). Must preserve semantics for role/name/content, assistant function_call behavior, stop sequences, temperature/top_p controls, message chunking, and streaming chunk shapes. Should avoid breaking existing Redwood APIs and keep performance overhead minimal.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming ChatCompletions request can be proxied to Redwood generation with identical behavior for: role/name/message order, stop sequences, temperature/top_p, max_tokens.
Streaming responses emit OpenAI-compatible 'delta' chunks including function_call.name and content deltas in the same order clients expect.

Function/tool calling: when model signals a function_call, the compatibility layer should surface name, arguments (as a single JSON string) to Redwood tooling hooks and return the function result back to the client formatted as OpenAI does.

Structured outputs: when callers specify JSON schema or format instructions via messages, the translator must forward these as Redwood structured-output constraints and verify final outputs conform to requested schema, returning a schema-validation error in OpenAI-compatible format if violated.
Latency regression < 10% added p95 compared to native Redwood API for same model and request shape.
Comprehensive unit and integration tests for streaming/non-streaming, function-calling, and schema-enforced outputs with sample payloads from common OSS clients.
notes: Decision: implement translator as an edge middleware component in the API gateway to minimize changes to runtime.
Trade-off: doing full request canonicalization at gateway increases header parsing cost but avoids touching runtime kernel logic.
Schema validation lib chosen: ajv (fast, widely used) — will wrap errors into OpenAI-compatible error codes.
Fallback behavior: if translation fails, return 400 with OpenAI-like error body and include original request id for support.
Upper bound for per-request CPU budget: 10ms median additional CPU time; if hotspots appear, move heavy work to async preflight service.

implementation_plan: Phase 1 — mapping matrix and unit tests: define canonical translation for fields and streaming chunk format.
Phase 2 — gateway middleware: implement translator for non-streaming requests and responses; add tests and feature flag.
Phase 3 — streaming re-chunker: implement streaming delta emission and backwards-compatible ordering guarantees.
Phase 4 — schema validation and function_call bridging: integrate ajv, wire function_call arguments to internal tooling hook, add error translations.
Phase 5 — perf and canary rollout: benchmark, optimize hot paths, canary to 5% of hosted traffic, monitor regressions and rollback plan.
risks: Potential incompatibility with some third-party clients that rely on non-standard chunk ordering.
Increased load at API gateway could become a bottleneck; autoscaling policies may need tuning.
Edge cases: nested function_call arguments larger than typical tokenize budgets; must ensure streaming doesn't break with very large JSON arguments.
review_feedback: Design review 2026-03-12: Add explicit mapping for message 'name' to ensure assistant/user bot names preserved.
Security review requested — ensure argument strings are not logged; use redact rules in gateway.
qa_notes: Include automated fuzz tests that simulate partial/incomplete function_call streams.
Run nightly end-to-end tests with popular OSS clients (OpenAI python sdk, node-openai) to detect regressions.
